title: Type casting: implicit and explicit

stages.name: 1. The two values
stages.detail: total = 7 and count = 2. Both are int.

stages.name: 2. The cast
stages.detail: (double) total makes a temporary decimal copy: 7.0. The variable total itself does not change.

stages.name: 3. Mixed types
stages.detail: 7.0 (double) divided by 2 (int). C++ automatically changes the 2 to 2.0.

visuals.title: Match the expression to its result

pairs.meaning: 3 (int / int: the decimal part is dropped)
3.5 (one decimal operand makes it a decimal division)
3 (cast too late: the division was already done as int)

goal: After this you can predict when C++ changes a type by itself, and use (double)x or static_cast<double>(x) to get a decimal answer.
warmup: Your exam marks are 78, 85 and 90. The total is 253. If you divide 253 by 3 on paper, you get 84.33. A basic calculator that only knows whole numbers would say 84. Type casting is how you tell C++ to use the decimal calculator.
definition: Type casting means converting a value from one data type to another. Implicit conversion happens automatically, for example in 2 + 3.5 the int 2 becomes the double 2.0. Explicit casting is when you ask for the change yourself, with (double) x or static_cast<double>(x). A cast creates a converted copy; it does not change the original variable.
howItWorks: Step through the trace and watch the types in the boxes. Remember the rule: when an int meets a double, the int is promoted to double and the answer is double. But if int meets int the answer stays int, even if you store it in a double afterwards. So cast BEFORE the division, not after.
syntax:
double d = (double) x;               // C-style cast
double d = static_cast<double>(x);   // C++ style cast (preferred)
int n = (int) 9.87;                  // 9: decimal part is cut off, not rounded

double avg = (double) total / count; // cast total FIRST, then divide
double bad = (double)(total / count);// too late: int division already done

char c = 'A';
int code = c;                        // 65 (implicit: char to int)
char next = static_cast<char>(c + 1);// 'B'

sample.title: Integer division, then casts

explanation.text: Two int variables: 7 and 2.
total / count is int / int, so the result is the int 3. Only then is 3 stored in the double (as 3.0). The decimal part is already lost.
(double) total turns a copy of total into 7.0 first. Then 7.0 / 2 is a decimal division: 3.5.
The same idea written the C++ way: static_cast<double>(total).
Casting a decimal to int cuts off the decimal part (no rounding): 9.87 becomes 9.
A double with no decimal part prints as 3.

steps.note: int / int = 3 (the .5 is lost). Then 3 is stored in a double, so avg1 holds 3.0.
(double) total makes a temporary 7.0. A double divided by an int is done as double: 3.5.
static_cast<double>(total) does the same as the C-style cast: 3.5.
The cast (int) cuts off .87. No rounding happens, so n = 9.
A double 3.0 is printed as 3; 3.5 stays 3.5.

sample.title: char and int are friends

explanation.text: A char stores a letter. Inside the computer, 'A' is the number 65.
Storing a char in an int converts it automatically. code is 65.
ch + 1 is 66. Storing it back into a char makes the letter 'B'.
Prints the number 65.
A char variable prints as a letter: B.
ch + 1 is an int (66), so cout prints a number, not a letter.
The cast turns 67 back into a char, so it prints C.
Casting the letter 'a' to int shows its code: 97.

steps.note: Implicit conversion: the char becomes the int 65.
ch + 1 = 66, stored in a char, so it is the letter B.
code is an int, so it prints 65.
next is a char, so it prints the letter.
ch + 1 is an int expression, so it prints 66.
Cast 67 to char: the letter C.

sample.title: Average of three marks

explanation.text: Marks in three subjects.
The sum of three ints is an int: 253.
253 / 3 is int / int, so the answer is cut to 84 before it goes into the double.
The cast makes a decimal copy of sum first, so the division is done in double: 84.3333.
Prints the wrong (cut) average.
Prints the correct average. cout shows 6 digits by default.

steps.note: 253 / 3 as int division is 84. Stored in a double: 84.0.
Print the correct average (cout shows about 6 digits).

variations.when: C++ changes the type itself, usually int to double or char to int
C-style explicit cast (old style, still common in notes)
C++ style explicit cast (preferred, easy to search for)
Decimal into int: the decimal part is cut off silently
char to int: you get the character code
Turn a number back into a letter

mistakes.error: No error, but the answer is wrong: sum / 3 is already int division, so the cast is too late.
expected '(' before 'x' (static_cast needs brackets around the value)

mistakes.wrong: double avg = total / count;   // total = 7, count = 2
mistakes.error: No error, but avg is 3, not 3.5. Storing in a double does not rescue int division.
No error. Casting cuts the decimal part (9). It does not round.

examTips: int / int is always int. Putting the answer in a double does not bring the decimals back.
Cast one operand BEFORE the division: (double) a / b, not (double)(a / b).
Casting to int cuts off the decimal part. It does not round: (int) 9.99 is 9.
A cast gives a converted copy. The original variable keeps its own type and value.
Know both styles: (double) x and static_cast<double>(x). Exams may use either.
romanSummary: Type casting ka matlab ek data type ko doosre type mein badalna.
Implicit conversion automatic hoti hai, jaise 2 + 3.5 mein int 2 double ban jata hai.
Explicit casting khud likhni parti hai: (double) x ya static_cast<double>(x).
int / int ka jawab int hi hota hai, isliye division se PEHLE cast karo: (double) total / count.
(int) 9.87 ka jawab 9 hai, round nahi hota, decimal hissa kat jata hai.

practice.explanation: int / double is done as double, so the answer is 3.5.
Casting to int cuts the decimal part, so 9.87 becomes 9.

practice.hint: Which cast happens before the division?
practice.explanation: Checked on a real run: int division is 3; casting a first gives 3.5; casting after the division gives 3 (shown as 3).
ch + 1 is the int 66. (char)(ch + 2) turns 67 back into the letter C.

practice.hint: Where is the cast placed relative to the division?
practice.explanation: The division happens inside the bracket as int / int. Move the cast to a so the division becomes a decimal division.

practice.prompt: Fill in the blank so the result is a decimal: double avg = ______<double>(sum) / 3;
practice.hint: It is the C++ style cast.
practice.explanation: static_cast<double>(sum) converts a copy of sum to double before dividing.

practice.hint: cout shows about 6 digits in total for a double.
practice.explanation: wrong is 253 / 3 = 84 by int division. right is 253.0 / 3 = 84.3333 (six significant digits).

quiz.hint: Implicit means it happens by itself.
quiz.explanation: In 2 + 3.5 the int is promoted to double automatically.
The decimal part is cut off, so it is 3.

quiz.prompt: Which line gives avg = 3.5 when total = 7 and count = 2?
quiz.explanation: Only this line makes a decimal division. The others divide two ints first.

quiz.prompt: What is the correct C++ style cast of x to double?
quiz.hint: It has a keyword, angle brackets and round brackets.
quiz.explanation: static_cast<type>(value) is the C++ style cast.
'A' is 65, so c + 1 is the int 66, and cout prints it as a number.
